raw.thesis: Narma is introducing an "Enterprise Agentic Brain" for AI-first companies. The core innovation lies in its three-layered architecture: Observe, Intelligence, and Execution. It focuses on understanding existing work patterns through lightweight desktop sensors (Observe), identifying intent, business value, and "drift" in workflows via a central "Brain" (Intelligence Layer), and then autonomously creating and deploying AI agents for high-ROI opportunities (Execution Layer). This is not about building new LLMs, but about leveraging existing foundation models to analyze a "Work Graph" — essentially, how work *actually* gets done – to pinpoint inefficiencies and automate tasks mid-flow. This venture is for AI-first companies who are struggling to measure the ROI of AI, understand where their resources are being spent, and combat "drift" in their automated and human processes. Narma aims to provide continuous AI-driven improvement by observing work, deciding AI actions, and building agents automatically. The founder envisions a future of "Continuous AI lift." The founder has not specified a goal type (lifestyle, growth, moonshot), but the ambition of "Continuous AI lift" and "AI automation at scale" suggests a growth or moonshot trajectory rather than a lifestyle business. The venture is currently at the idea stage, as no artifacts or signals were mentioned, and the description focuses on the conceptual architecture and vision.

raw.product_description: Narma is an "Enterprise Agentic Brain" with a three-layer architecture: Observe (desktop sensors for work patterns), Intelligence (a "Brain" detecting intent, business value, and drift), and Execution (an "Agent Factory" for generating and deploying AI agents). It leverages existing foundation models, focusing on a "Work Graph" to identify and automate high-ROI tasks for continuous AI improvement.
